@graph.name: Stuffed Poblano Peppers
@graph.description: These stuffed poblano peppers are hearty and delicious! This protein-rich recipe is vegetarian and gluten-free, so everyone can enjoy it. Recipe yields 6 stuffed peppers.
recipeIngredient: 2 cans (15 ounces each) black beans, reserve ¼ cup cooking liquid, then drain but do not rinse
1 chipotle chili in adobo sauce, plus 1 teaspoon adobo sauce
½ cup fresh cilantro, plus more for garnish
1 tablespoon olive oil, for brushing, plus more for greasing the pan
1 ½ cups (6 ounces) shredded Monterey Jack cheese
½ cup (2 ounces) crumbled Cotija or feta cheese
For serving: cooked brown rice (optional), sour cream, cilantro lime sauce or guacamole

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees Fahrenheit. Lightly grease a 9 by 13-inch pan with olive oil or cooking spray.
To make the black bean puree: In a small skillet over medium heat, toast the cumin and coriander, stirring often until fragrant, about 1 minute.

Transfer the spices to a food processor. Add the beans and reserved liquid, chipotle chili and adobo sauce, lime juice, and salt. Process until smooth, scraping the bowl as needed. Add the cilantro and blend for a few seconds, until it’s broken up into tiny bits. Set it aside for now.

Pour about ⅔ cup of the salsa into the prepared baking dish, and tilt it from side to side until the bottom of the dish is evenly coated. Cut a slit down the length of each poblano. Use your fingers and a paring knife to remove (and then discard) the membranes and seeds from each pepper. Arrange the peppers in the baking dish with the cut side facing up, and brush them all over with oil.

In a bowl, combine the shredded cheese, crumbled cheese and lime juice. Stir to combine. Use a spoon to fill most of each pepper with the pureed beans, then stuff a handful of cheese inside. Drizzle the remaining salsa back and forth over the peppers.

Bake for 40 to 45 minutes, until the tops are roasted and golden and the pepper is tender all around. Serve peppers warm, with a dollop of sour cream and a sprinkle of cilantro on top. Leftover peppers keep well in the refrigerator, covered, for up to 4 days—gently reheat them in the microwave or at 350 degrees Fahrenheit until warmed through.

review.reviewBody: This is a great recipe. Is there a reason that you do not roast and peel the poblanos first? I live in Mexico and this step is never skipped with traditional recipes. I am a huge fan of yours and have delighted making your recipes for quite a while. Thank you

I have never left a recipe review, but this recipe is so good. I just had to do it. I have never made any of the recipes from this site that were not good, but this one was outstanding. The combination of flavor and texture left me wanting to eat more even after I was full. I am not a vegetarian, but I could easily quit eating meat with the recipes on your site. It is my favorite place to go to find great recipes to make. Thank you, Kate. Well done!

I’ve been waiting to make this recipe since I saw it posted recently and finally got around to it last night. It was absolutely delicious! 

I used a store bought mild salsa made with roasted tomatoes this time. I also didn’t have coriander so used finely chopped cilantro with a dash of curry powder for that, along with the cumin. (For anyone else out there who, like me, usually doesn’t stray from  recipes as written )

My husband and I both now have it as one of our favorite dishes of yours  ⭐️

Made this tonight, sort of.  I got part way into the recipe when I realized I had neither black beans nor lime juice, 2 ingredients I always have on hand.  Since I had already started, I substituted 1 can red kidney beans and 1 can navy beans for the beans and 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar for the lime.  The recipe was still delicious (but would have been much better with the lime).  I can't wait to make it again correctly!  Easy, filling, yummy!

This was sooo tasty!  
I sautéed some frozen corn with chopped red onion and jalapeños to serve on the side.
Excellent!
I made these last night and they were great! It definitely took longer to prep than the recipe says. But they were delicious and I will make them again!

Incredible flavour, and so easy to make. I love chile relleno, and this is all the goodness, but without deep frying. My only deviation was to use 1 cup dried black beans, boiled, to sub the 2 tins of beans. Served over rice with a dollop of sour cream, and it was bliss. Definitely a keeper.

I was not impressed with this recipe.  First of all, only one can of black beans would have been sufficient.  The recipe made more than enough to fill the poblanos with lots left over.  And I felt the recipe didn't have enough flavor and was too time consuming to justify the end product.  The end result did not look like the photo on your website and lacked flavor.  Not a good use of my favorite poblanos.

Made this for breakfast and it was fabulous! I didn't have fresh cilantro so I added 1 tsp. dried cilantro instead.  I omitted the chipotle and adobo sauce to make it milder, but it was deliciously spicy anyhow. 

Served it with sour cream and roasted potato slices. Would cook this again.
This is a delicious recipe as written. Thank you for this perfect Sunday dish, Kate. As close to meatless perfect as it gets.

Recipe is great as presented. But to save time, I have made this with store-bought salsa (Mateo's or Trader Joe's basic red), halved and stemmed/de-seeded the poblanos and microwaved them for 2-3 minutes to soften them, then proceeded with the recipe for about 15-20 minutes less oven time. I found that the beans could be pureed with an immersion blender, and I have also mixed rice into the beans (no need for a side of rice) b/c my poblanos happened to be on the big side. If you like spice and don't have a lime around, you could put a few pickled onions/jalapenos in the bean mixture for some acidity.... As always, Kate brings the good whole-foods recipes. Thank you!
